A year ago, I came to know that I had a uterine fibroid. Initially it was quite small, but gradually it started increasing significantly, especially after my father’s demise. Over the next eight months, I consulted around 8–9 doctors. Most of them suggested that since I am 43 years old and there is a history of cancer in my family, I should undergo removal of my uterus and even sacrifice my ovaries. However, I strongly believed that my ovaries should be preserved, and I struggled for months trying to make the right decision.

Finally, a friend suggested Dr. Imran Hamza Wala. I had a video consultation with him, and from the very first interaction, I felt reassured. He explained the entire procedure with such clarity and confidence that all my doubts slowly disappeared. He assured me that he was not in favor of removing my uterus or ovaries unnecessarily, which aligned with my own thoughts and gave me immense comfort.

My surgery was initially planned for 19th May, as I had gone on a trip to Bali in the first week of May. Unfortunately, during the trip I experienced excruciating pain and had to consult a doctor there, who advised immediate surgery. I cancelled the remainder of my trip and flew back to Mumbai, where my robotic surgery was performed at Safi Hospital by Dr. Imran Hamza Wala.

I can genuinely say that I have never met a doctor like him. He is exceptionally skilled, talented, transparent, and incredibly knowledgeable. He explains every procedure as if he is teaching you, making you visualize and understand every step. His calm and polite demeanor gives you so much confidence that even a major surgery starts feeling like just another process.

What stood out the most was the way he guided me before and after surgery—his prompt responses, care, patience, and personal attention were unlike anything I had experienced before. After the surgery, he even showed me the surgical video and explained every detail to me, which was something entirely new and truly remarkable.

I feel extremely grateful and blessed to have met a doctor like Dr. Imran Hamza Wala. My entire family is deeply impressed by him and his team. I sincerely pray that God blesses him and creates more doctors like him—doctors who not only treat patients but also give them confidence, comfort, and hope.

Thank you, Dr. Imran Hamza Wala and your entire team.

God bless you always.

Our journey with Dr. Saloni Suchak has been nothing short of a blessing. We began consulting her even before pregnancy, and from that very first day until the last moment of our nine-month journey, she stood with us not just as a doctor, but as someone who felt like a part of our family. Her warmth, her patience, and the genuine care she showed made us feel safe, supported, and understood at every step.

Throughout these nine months, we faced many questions, fears, and emotional moments, but Dr. Saloni always had a calming smile and reassuring words that gave us courage. She held our hands through every ultrasound, every doubt, and every worry. The comfort she gave us cannot be measured in words.

But it was the day of delivery when we truly understood the meaning of dedication, compassion, and humanity in a doctor.

My wife went into early labor, and we had always hoped for a normal delivery. Dr. Saloni knew this and respected our wish with her whole heart. When the labor began, the pain became unbearable for my wife, and she struggled to push. For more than an hour, Dr. Saloni and her team stood by her side, motivating her every single second. She didn’t treat us like patients—she treated us like her own people.

She kept coming out of the labor room to talk to us, giving us hope when we had almost lost it. Her words felt like strength at a time when we were breaking down from worry. She explained gently that the baby was in a perfect position for a normal delivery, and she wanted to honour our wish as long as it was safe.

When things became critical and she shifted my wife to the OT for a C-section, our hearts sank. But even there, Dr. Saloni, along with a team of 4–5 doctors and 7–8 nurses, gave one final attempt for a normal delivery. The amount of effort, teamwork, and emotional support we witnessed in that room is something we will remember for the rest of our lives.

After more than 2.5 hours of extreme labour, our healthy baby boy finally arrived — and at that moment, we understood that it was not just a medical success, but a miracle created by Dr. Saloni and her team.

Today, both mother and baby are perfectly fine, and this would not have been possible without her dedication, her skill, and her huge heart.

Dr. Saloni Suchak is not just a doctor—she is a guardian angel for expecting parents. We are forever grateful to her for giving us the biggest happiness of our lives and for treating us with such humanity and love.
